prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and figures (ideological framing removed)

Health and social care
- NHS: Additional revenue spend rising to £28bn/year by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years; reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry with funding up to £3bn/year by 2030; primary care funding +£1.5bn/year by 2030 and £2bn capital; invest in diagnostics; restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn).
- Workforce: Support pay restoration for junior doctors; immediate budget increases to settle NHS pay.
- Mental health: Access to evidence-based therapies within 28 days; tailored provision; a paid counsellor in every school and sixth-form college.
- Cancer: National plan to meet 75% early diagnosis by 2028; prevention; public research.
- Assisted dying: Support legal change with safeguards.
- HIV: End new transmissions by 2030; expand opt-out testing.

Social care and disability
- Free personal care; £20bn/year investment; national pay, terms and career structure for carers; visa reform to prevent exploitation; “Care Supporter” right.
- Disability: +5% to disability benefits; oppose PIP vouchers; reform assessments; mandatory free transport for 16–18 SEND students; workplace support.
- Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; extend “staying put”; guaranteed counselling.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes per year; end Right to Buy; rent controls via local authorities; end Section 21; long-term leases.
- Standards: Passivhaus-equivalent for new homes; solar and low-carbon heat mandatory; upgrade PRS to EPC C.
- Retrofit (5 years): £29bn for homes (to EPC B), £4bn for public buildings, £9bn for low-carbon heat, £7bn for heat adaptation; street-by-street delivery via councils.
- Empty homes powers; first-refusal for social landlords on certain sales; stronger public building control; whole-life carbon in planning.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax starting £120/tCO2, rising to up to £500 within 10 years.
- Renewables: End onshore wind barriers; targets by 2035—80 GW offshore wind, 53 GW onshore, 100 GW solar; wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; community ownership thresholds; Crown Estate in public ownership; grid expansion, interconnectors, storage; regulate bioenergy (end wood imports for Drax, end biomass subsidies).
- Nuclear: Stop new build; phase out existing.

Economy and taxation
- Green investment: Average £40bn/year (rail electrification, public transport, buildings retrofit, industry decarbonisation, water/sewage, adaptation).
- Public ownership: Rail, water, Big 5 retail energy companies.
- Tax changes: Wealth tax 1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn; align CGT and investment income rates with earned income; remove NI upper earnings limit; reform inheritance and pension relief; revalue Council Tax; steps toward Land Value Tax; windfall taxes on oil/gas and banks; VAT changes (reduce for hospitality/arts; increase for financial services/private education).
- Carbon tax revenue up to ~£80bn by end of parliament (then declining); personal tax reforms raise £50–70bn/year by end of parliament; borrow to invest within inflation capacity.
- SMEs: Regional mutual banks (capitalised incl. £10bn public funds); £2bn/year local grants to decarbonise; Prompt Payment Code in law.

Work and welfare
- Workers’ rights: Repeal anti-union laws; day-one rights; single “worker” status for gig economy; 10:1 pay ratio; £15 minimum wage (all ages) with higher Employment Allowance; equal pay audits; move toward four-day week.
- Social security: +£40/week to UC/legacy benefits; end five-week wait; scrap two-child cap and bedroom tax; +10%/month Carer’s Allowance; maintain triple lock; end sanctions; long-term UBI ambition.

Nature, animals, food
- 30% land/sea protected by 2030; Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; re-wet peat; expand woodland/scrub/hedgerows; £3bn/year grants; Right to Roam (England); water nationalisation; DEFRA +£1.5bn; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Animal welfare: Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics); end badger cull; restrict biofuels; ban lead ammo; modernise dog laws; reduce animal testing.
- Food: Triple farm support to transition to nature-friendly farming; link payments to pesticide reduction; expand domestic horticulture; strengthen Groceries Code; all children to receive free school meals and breakfast (to Y6); food education; local food funds.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn teacher pay); £2.5bn/year for safe buildings; end high-stakes testing and abolish Ofsted; equal status for arts/vocational; Natural History GCSE; academies/free schools to LA control; remove private schools’ charitable status and apply VAT (exempt SEN places).
- Early years: £1.4bn/year for Sure Start; extend childcare to 35 hours/week from 9 months (sector-negotiated).
- SEND: +£5bn for mainstream inclusion and transport.
- Post-16/FE: +£3bn for sixth forms; £12bn for skills/lifelong learning; restore EMA.
- HE: Scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; address TPS impacts.

Transport
- Public transport: Subsidies to £10bn/year; £19bn over five years for public transport and active travel; rail nationalisation; local bus control; £2.5bn/year for walking/cycling.
- Roads: No new road building; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; EV scrappage up to £5bn/year; end new petrol/diesel sales by 2027; end use by 2035; weight-based VED; default 20 mph in built-up areas; shift HGVs to rail.
- Aviation: Frequent-flyer levy; ban domestic flights where rail <3 hours; apply carbon tax to kerosene; no airport expansion; worker transition.

Democracy, migration, rights
- Electoral: Proportional representation; repeal Elections Act 2022 (voter ID); replace Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; transparency on lobbying/think tank funding; state party funding.
- Human rights: Protect HRA/ECHR; restore legal aid; scrap Police/Crime/Public Order Acts; trans self-ID; X passport marker; scrap Prevent; support religious expression.
- Migration: End hostile environment and NRPF; fast, fair asylum with safe routes and right to work; end 10-year route; limit detention; split Home Office; fee-at-cost; free NHS access; end spouse minimum income rule; voting rights for visa holders.

Justice and drugs
- Policing: End routine stop-and-search and facial recognition; diversity competency assessments; local oversight.
- Courts: +£11bn over parliament; recruit judges; repair courts; restore legal aid.
- Sentencing: Presumption against custodial sentences under two years; expand diversion and restorative justice.
- VAWG: Make misogyny a hate crime; fund local services; decriminalise sex work.
- Drugs: National commission; decriminalise personal possession with health-led diversion.

Foreign policy and defence
- Support Ukraine; strengthen international law; rejoin EU when feasible (steps: Customs Union, free movement, Erasmus).
- Aid/climate finance: Aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss and Damage; debt relief; ecocide law support.
- Trade: Remove ISDS-type systems; uphold labour/animal/environment standards.
- Nuclear/NATO: Sign TPNW; cancel Trident and dismantle UK nuclear weapons; push NATO no-first-use; prioritise diplomacy.
